items.title: DPIIT Launches 6th Edition of National Startup Awards to Recognise Innovation and Entrepreneurship
items.summary: The year 2026 marks the completion of ten years of the Startup India initiative, launched in January 2016 to build a strong, inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country.

facts.text: Since its inception in 2019, the National Startup Awards have emerged as a flagship initiative under Startup India, providing a national platform to recognise entrepreneurial excellence and showcase innovative solutions addressing critical challenges across sectors.

NSA 6.0 will recognise innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence across 20 sectoral categories and three special award categories, reflecting India’s evolving startup ecosystem, emerging technologies and national development priorities.
Introduced for the first time, the student award aims to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among school and college students across all 36 States and Union Territories.

Winning startups across the 20 sectoral categories and the two startup-focused special categories will be eligible for a cash prize of ₹25 lakh per category, subject to the applicable award guidelines.

items.title: Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas
items.summary: The rule will come into effect from 01 st November 2026. The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits.

facts.text: The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits.

Under the new provision, eligible non-commercial vehicle owners with a valid and functional FASTag, residing within 20 km range can choose between the existing monthly pass and the concessional Local Pass for commuting through a specific fee plaza.
The amendment has been notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the powers conferred by the National Highways Act, 1956.

With over 13 crore FASTags issued across the country, the new provision aims to provide an option for eligible residents living near toll plazas to make travel more economical and enhance Ease of Commuting for local residents.

Carbon dioxide is increasingly being viewed not only as an emission, but also as a potential resource. CCUS can support India’s Net Zero by 2070 vision while strengthening industrial competitiveness and resource efficiency.

facts.text: Powering India's Industries Towards a Net Zero Future 27 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi CCUS is an important pathway for reducing emissions from hard-to-abate sectors.
India’s journey towards Net Zero by 2070 requires reducing emissions across its energy and industrial sectors.
NITI Aayog identifies CCUS as critical for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors , including steel, cement, oil and gas, petrochemicals, chemicals and fertilisers.
The Department of Science and Technology’s CCUS Roadmap 2025 identifies potential industrial and geological regions for such clusters.
